newsitem.title: GERMANY: Most Germans believe in advertising -- survey.
newsitem.headline: Most Germans believe in advertising -- survey.

text.p: More than half of Germans find advertising believable, according to an opinion poll by an industry association published on Thursday.
Some 58 percent of the 2,500 Germans polled said they found advertising credible, a rate which has climbed continuously since 1994, the Deutscher Fachverlag (DFV) said in its publication Horizont.
Women tended to believe in advertising more readily than men, and west Germans more than east Germans.

In western Germany, the number who found advertising believable rose to 59.6 percent in 1996 from 56.6 percent in 1994. But in eastern Germany, where around a fifth of Germans live, the proportion fell to 52.6 in 1996 from 57 percent two years earlier.

The DFV said daily newspaper spots were ranked more believable than those on television. Forty-four percent of respondents said they trusted newspapers more, versus 37 percent who favoured television ads.
